newsitem.title: USA: Trade Center trial start postponed for a day. [CORRECTED 19:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Trade Center trial start postponed for a day. [CORRECTED 19:54 GMT]

text.p: Opening arguments in the trial of the accused mastermind in the 1993 World Trade Centre bombing were postponed on Monday due to the illness of one juror and the dismissal of an alternate juror.

The trial of Ramzi Yousef and his co-defendant Eyad Ismoil had been scheduled to start just days after authorities said they had prevented a suicide bombing attack on the New York subway by Middle Eastern men. Officials say there is no apparent link between those arrested and Yousef.
U.S. District Court Judge Kevin Duffy said one of the 12 permanent jurors had called in sick but was expected to be in court on Tuesday.
Duffy removed the first alternate juror from the trial because of the possibility someone could identify him.
"He said something which compromised his status as an anonymous juror," Duffy said in Manhattan federal court.

At the request of defence lawyers, Duffy questioned all of the permanent jurors and each of the six alternate jurors about whether their impartiality had been affected by last week's suicide bombing in Israel and the discovery of five pipe bombs in a raid on a Brooklyn apartment.
The judge said opening arguments would begin on Tuesday if he and lawyers were satisfied that the juror who was absent on Monday could remain fair.

Security was tightened around New York and there was a blaze of publicity surrounding last Thursday's raid in Brooklyn. Authorities charged two men with planning to bomb the subway and a third man arrested was being held on immigration charges.

Hundreds of people were evacuated from the World Trade Centre Monday (correcting day from Tuesday to Monday) morning when a suspicious package was reported. It turned out to be a broken musical greeting card, police sources said.

Yousef, who claims Palestinian and Pakistani ancestry, is accused of planning and planting the 1,200 pound (545 kilogram) fertiliser bomb that exploded Feb. 26, 1993, killing six people and injuring more than 1,000 others in the 110-story twin towers.
Ismoil, a Jordanian, is accused of driving the van that carried the bomb into the trade centre basement garage.

Yousef was indicted in 1993 on charges of taking part in the trade centre bombing, along with four Moslem fundamentalists who were convicted in 1994. The four were each sentenced to 240 years in prison for their roles in the devastating explosion.

Prosecutors say Yousef fled the country on a plane to Karachi, Pakistan, just hours after the blast. Yousef was one of the world's most wanted fugitives, with a $2 million bounty on his head, until his February 1995 arrest in Pakistan.
In September 1996, Yousef and two other radical Moslems were convicted of planning to bomb 12 U.S. passenger jets over the Pacific Ocean to punish the United States for its support of Israel.
Duffy said after a four-day hearing last week that he would not bar government scientific experts from testifying about chemical residue found during the extensive probe.

Defence lawyers wanted the testimony excluded at the trial after a highly publicised report by the Justice Department's inspector general last April criticised the FBI's handling of the case in their crime laboratories.
